browse.decadeIntro.earlier: Music from earlier centuries lives on through songs, instrumental works and performances passed down across generations. Explore the recordings that connect your collection with this period.
browse.decadeIntro.future: The music of this decade is still ahead of us. Explore releases associated with these future years in your collection.
browse.decadeIntro.general: Discover the music your collection connects with these years, from familiar styles to new directions and distinctive voices.
browse.decadeIntro.nineteenthCentury: Concert halls, opera houses and music at home shaped this era of classical and Romantic music. Recordings in your collection may revisit works written long before recording became widespread.
browse.decadeIntro.y1900: Ragtime, brass bands and parlour songs filled theatres and homes, while cylinders and early discs carried performers to new listeners. In concert music, late Romantic richness met new approaches to harmony and colour.
browse.decadeIntro.y1910: Ragtime and dance bands shared the stage with early blues and, by 1917, the first jazz recordings. Concert music broke with tradition through bold rhythms and unfamiliar harmonies, and Tin Pan Alley songs travelled widely as sheet music.
browse.decadeIntro.y1920: Jazz, blues and dance orchestras reached growing audiences through records and the new medium of radio. Improvising soloists and expressive singers came to the fore, alongside the first country recordings, Broadway songs and adventurous concert music.
browse.decadeIntro.y1930: Big-band swing brought dance rhythms, memorable singers and inventive soloists to a wide audience. Film musicals, blues, gospel and country found loyal followings, and Latin rhythms such as the rumba found eager dancers.
browse.decadeIntro.y1940: Bebop gave jazz a fast, adventurous language as the swing era wound down. Jump blues fed into rhythm and blues, bluegrass took shape and crooners lent popular song a softer intimacy.
browse.decadeIntro.y1950: Rock and roll carried the energy of rhythm and blues and country to teenage audiences through radio and 45 rpm singles. Doo-wop, electric blues, mambo and modern jazz thrived as well, and the long-playing record gave albums room to grow.
browse.decadeIntro.y1960: Pop and rock became a space for rapid experimentation, from the British beat boom and folk-rock to psychedelic studio sounds. Soul, bossa nova, free jazz and the folk revival added a wealth of other voices.
browse.decadeIntro.y1970: Funk and disco filled dance floors, progressive rock stretched the album format and punk brought a sharper edge. Reggae, heavy metal, singer-songwriters and jazz fusion found large audiences, while early hip-hop and electronic experiments pointed ahead.
browse.decadeIntro.y1980: Synth-pop, new wave and the first house and techno tracks grew around synthesisers, drum machines and sampling. Music videos and portable cassette players changed how songs were seen and heard, as hip-hop widened its reach and rock and metal filled arenas.
browse.decadeIntro.y1990: Grunge, alternative rock and Britpop gave guitar music fresh directions, while hip-hop and R&B became major creative forces. House, techno and drum and bass filled clubs and raves, and CD reissues put older recordings back into circulation.
browse.decadeIntro.y2000: Hip-hop, R&B, pop, indie rock and electronic music shared an increasingly digital world. Downloads, digital music players and music blogs changed how listeners discovered songs, opening new routes for independent artists.
browse.decadeIntro.y2010: Streaming and playlists changed everyday listening, bringing music from many places within easy reach. Pop, hip-hop and electronic dance music crossed paths, K-pop and Latin pop reached charts worldwide and independent artists built audiences online.
browse.decadeIntro.y2020: Streaming and short video clips connect pop, hip-hop and electronic music with regional scenes around the world. New releases sit alongside rediscovered recordings, bringing fresh voices and older favourites into the same listening space.

export.panel.intro: Download the loaded iBroadcast library as structured JSON or a ZIP of linked CSV tables. Includes separate album artists, track credits, roles, credit phrases, genres, ratings and upload dates. Uses the full loaded library, regardless of page filters.
export.panel.snapshot: This snapshot contains saved metadata; open drafts and later changes are not included. Audio and image files are not included.

gapless.settings.enable: Enable gapless playback for albums in order
gapless.settings.formats: Use Original streaming quality (Premium) for consecutive FLAC album tracks: mono or stereo, 16/24-bit, 8–192 kHz, with compatible formats and decoder block sizes. Supported FLAC is repackaged without altering its audio samples. MP3 is experimental, requires reliable encoder timing metadata and is decoded to 24-bit PCM; sample alignment across real MP3 streams has not been established. Unsupported files or transitions use standard playback. No crossfade or automatic silence removal is used.
gapless.settings.heading: Gapless playback
gapless.settings.intro: Keep consecutive album tracks playing without an added pause. Off by default. Only for normal album order; not shuffle, Random Album, playlists or queue sync. Your choice is remembered in this browser and applies on the next track.
gapless.settings.limits: The current file is prepared first. Longer tracks can start while the next downloads; very short runs prepare one extra track before starting. Buffer and preparation limits may switch to standard playback. The track-based time bar keeps the continuous buffer underneath. Volume and playback speed remain available in Playback options or Sound. Slow connections and incompatible files can still interrupt playback; this experiment does not guarantee uninterrupted output for every file or device.
gapless.settings.startup: Starting an album can take longer. Seeking near a track's end may show Preparing… while the current audio continues. Unsupported files use standard playback.
gapless.startPrepared: Press Play in Tagcast to start the prepared audio.
gapless.status.currentOnly: Gapless current track; next uses standard playback. {{reason}}
gapless.status.disabled: Standard playback selected; applies on the next track.
gapless.status.enabled: Gapless enabled; applies on the next track.
gapless.status.followingStandard: A following album track needs standard playback. {{reason}}
gapless.status.nextTransitionStandard: Gapless current track; next transition uses standard playback. {{reason}}
gapless.status.seekPreparing: Preparing the next album track before seeking…
gapless.status.unsupported: Gapless buffering is unavailable in this browser; standard playback is retained.
gaplessSettings.diagnostics.memory: Use Activity Monitor for total app memory.
gaplessSettings.diagnostics.note: For reporting a playback problem in Tagcast. Off each time you open the app. Records anonymous queue positions, preparation and buffer timings, player events and fallback categories. No track names, account details, stream URLs or music are recorded. The latest {{limit, number}} events stay in memory until you explicitly download them or close the app.
gaplessSettings.diagnostics.started: Collecting anonymous playback events. Download after reproducing the problem.
gaplessSettings.diagnostics.stopped: Collection stopped. You can download the retained events; enabling again starts a new log.

help.album.edit.body: Edit opens a draft with online suggestions. Review the changes before saving. A multi-disc set also has an Edit disc option for each disc.
help.album.edit.title: Edit this album
help.album.intro.body: The breadcrumb returns to the browsing context where you opened this album, with its filters and position. The header shows the album artist, release year, track count and duration. Click a known year to browse releases from that year. Genre and tag chips stay together; + Tag opens tag management. Double-click a real cover to enlarge it. If About this album is available below the header, expand it to read the background text. Optional TheAudioDB album information is enabled separately in Settings, fetched only for the album you visit and saved locally for 30 days.
help.album.intro.title: Your album
help.album.lyrics.body: Choose More album actions (⋯) → Check album lyrics to read this album’s native lyrics one track at a time, up to 100 tracks. Results, including empty results, are saved locally for your account and survive restarts. Opening an album restores known labels from that local cache. Use Check iBroadcast again on a track to refresh changed text. Labels open known text without playback. Stop checking or leave the album to stop further reads. No LRCLIB searches or playlist checks run automatically.
help.album.lyrics.hint: Album lyrics checks need a connected account.
help.album.lyrics.title: Check album lyrics
help.album.play.body: Play album starts from the beginning and replaces the queue. Shuffle album replaces the queue with all tracks in a newly mixed order, including every disc of the set; each track plays once per pass. The displayed album order stays unchanged. The + menu offers Add to queue and Play next, preserving disc and track order. Add to playlist saves the album after a review.
help.album.play.title: Play or queue
help.album.ratings.body: Stars rate this album in iBroadcast. The heart saves a separate album favourite locally for your account, without changing its stars. Both apply to every disc of a multi-disc set.
help.album.ratings.hint: Album ratings are available with a connected iBroadcast account.
help.album.ratings.title: Album ratings
help.album.title: Album details
help.album.track.body: A track number becomes Play on hover or keyboard focus and starts listening from that track. The playing row has a speaker, or small moving bars with the player spectrum on, and a quiet highlight. Extra performers, composer credits and tags appear only when present; the album artist is not repeated. The heading shows the common file format; amber labels identify different formats. Row actions appear on hover or keyboard focus, and stay visible on touch devices. An active heart or thumbs-down stays visible. Hearts set the native track rating to 5, thumbs-down to 1; click the active control to clear it. Dislikes do not skip or trash tracks. Use # for track tags or + for queue and playlist actions.
help.album.track.title: Choose a track
help.album.trash.body: Open More album actions (⋯), then Move to trash to choose tracks. Duplicated marks repeated track numbers on the same disc, even when the titles differ. The album overview shows the same label. Upload dates and suggested keep/trash labels help compare copies: prefer FLAC over MP3, then the newest upload in the same format. Select suggested copies fills the checkboxes; uncertain versions remain manual. Select extra copies only chooses matching titles and keeps the first. Review the exact selection before confirming. Trashed tracks leave the library in every iBroadcast app.
help.album.trash.hint: Moving tracks to the trash is available with a connected account.
help.album.trash.title: Reviewed trash selection
help.albumFavourites.albums.body: Albums marked with a heart appear here, independently of their stars. These favourites are saved on this computer for your account. A multi-disc set appears once when all its discs are favourites.
help.albumFavourites.albums.title: Your favourite albums
help.albumFavourites.find.body: Search favourite albums by title or artist. Open a card to listen, change its stars or toggle its separate heart. Removing a favourite keeps its star rating and music.
help.albumFavourites.find.title: Find an album
help.albumFavourites.tabs.body: Favourites in the sidebar opens this shared page. Use Tracks, Albums or Album artists to switch lists without changing playback.
help.albumFavourites.tabs.title: Choose your favourites
help.albumFavourites.title: Album favourites
help.albumMerge.confirm.body: Nothing is written until you confirm. Tagcast checks membership and metadata again, sends one request and reads the result back. There is no automatic retry or Undo. An uncertain result requires reloading and checking iBroadcast; cancelling keeps your album selection.
help.albumMerge.confirm.title: Confirm once
help.albumMerge.keep.body: Merge 2–20 selected fragments of one disc into an existing destination, up to 500 tracks. Multi-disc sets and the iBroadcast Combine setting are blocked. Choose the destination explicitly; its album title, artists, year, disc number and rating are kept.
help.albumMerge.keep.title: Choose what to keep
help.albumMerge.title: Merge albums
help.albumMerge.tracks.body: Track IDs, titles, performers, credits, genres, artwork and numbers stay unchanged. Overlapping numbers require explicit confirmation; nothing is automatically renumbered or removed. Each track keeps its cover, so the displayed album image follows the first numbered track with artwork.
help.albumMerge.tracks.title: Review every track
help.albums.artistFavourites.body: On an album artist's page, the heart beside the name saves a local favourite for your account, independently of album hearts and stars. Artist biographies are optional in Settings. When enabled, only visited artists are looked up on TheAudioDB; text is cached locally and can be expanded in About this artist. Check the source when artists share a name.
help.albums.artistFavourites.hint: Open an album artist to use artist favourites. Enable optional biographies in Settings.
help.albums.artistFavourites.title: Artist favourites and biographies
help.albums.artistRating.body: The stars below an artist's name are their native iBroadcast rating, separate from the local heart and all album or track ratings. Choose one to save it; Clear removes it. Saving checks the previous value and reads the result back. Different artist ratings means this displayed name groups multiple native artists.
help.albums.artistRating.hint: Open an album artist to rate them.
help.albums.artistRating.title: Artist rating
help.albums.collection.body: These cards show your albums, or the albums by the artist you opened. Discs belonging to the same set are displayed together.
help.albums.collection.title: Your album collection
help.albums.open.body: Click a cover or title to open the album. Its small Play button starts the full album and replaces the queue. The + menu adds it to the queue or plays it next. Enlarge covers on the album page.
help.albums.open.title: Open, play or queue
help.albums.search.body: Search album titles, artists or genres. Filters opens the filter menu; the fixed buttons below the search field choose the order. Filters with no albums in the current artist scope are omitted; All albums remains available. Sort by name, release year, upload date or album rating. Random keeps one shuffled order while searching or paging; click Random again to reshuffle. Upload date uses the latest known active-track upload, including every disc in a set. Unknown dates and unrated albums stay last. Sorting never downloads tracks or starts playback.
help.albums.search.title: Search, filter and sort
help.albums.select.body: With a connected account, tick albums in the grid or list, including filtered results such as 1–2 tracks. Tag… opens the existing tag manager for all selected albums, including selections on other pages or outside the current results. Move selected albums to trash reviews all chosen albums and their tracks before confirmation. On an artist's page, you can also edit their selected albums together.
help.albums.select.title: Select or discover
help.albums.title: Albums
help.artistFavourites.artists.body: Artist hearts are saved on this computer for your account, independently of album hearts and stars. Open a card to see that artist’s albums. The heart beside their name adds or removes the artist favourite.
help.artistFavourites.artists.title: Your favourite album artists
help.artistFavourites.find.body: Search names, change their order or choose a page size. This list uses loaded album summaries and never downloads all track details.
help.artistFavourites.find.title: Find an artist
help.artistFavourites.tabs.body: Use the tabs to switch between favourite tracks, albums and album artists. Searches and pages stay separate; Back and Forward return to the previous list.
help.artistFavourites.tabs.title: Choose your favourites
help.artistFavourites.title: Favourite album artists
help.artists.browse.body: Each card groups the albums credited to one album artist. The totals refer to albums in your library.
help.artists.browse.title: Browse your album artists
help.artists.find.body: Search by name. The combined Filter and sort menu has separate Sort and Show sections: changing one keeps the other. Checkmarks identify both current choices. Empty filters are omitted; All album artists stays available. Sort by name, native artist rating or Random. Unrated artists stay last.
help.artists.find.title: Find an artist
help.artists.open.body: Choose an artist card to see their albums. On the artist page, hover or focus the larger photo to change it through the existing comparison; that action stays visible on touch devices. Back returns to this list with your search, order and page preserved. A filled heart identifies an artist favourite; choose Favourite artists in the filter to show only these artists.
help.artists.open.title: Open their albums
help.artists.pages.body: Choose how many artists to show per page, then use Previous and Next to move through the results.
help.artists.pages.title: Browse more artists
help.artists.title: Album artists
help.audioOutput.destination.body: System default follows your computer’s sound settings. This selection changes only this browser player; the same audio and queue keep running.
help.audioOutput.destination.title: Choose where to listen
help.audioOutput.devices.body: Choose output opens your browser’s device picker where supported. The list contains only outputs the browser makes available. Tagcast never requests microphone access to discover speakers. If no choices appear, use your system sound settings.
help.audioOutput.devices.title: Available devices
help.audioOutput.title: Sound
help.audioOutput.volume.body: The slider and Mute control the current player, even when your browser hides its own volume controls. Arrow keys adjust the focused slider. Your system or speaker may also have its own volume control. Playback and the queue stay in place.
help.audioOutput.volume.title: Adjust player volume
help.audioOutput.wireless.body: AirPlay appears only when your browser supports it and an output is available. It opens the native route picker. Otherwise, use your system sound settings for supported network speakers. Tagcast does not discover Sonos or Chromecast devices itself.
help.audioOutput.wireless.title: Wireless outputs
help.browseGroup.albums.body: An album appears when at least one track belongs to this group. Open an album to see its tracks or use its + menu to queue it.
help.browseGroup.albums.title: Albums in this group
help.browseGroup.find.body: Search and sort the matching albums here. The page size controls how many are displayed at once.
help.browseGroup.find.title: Find an album
help.browseGroup.play.body: Play random album chooses from all matching albums in this group, before pagination or sampling, and replaces the queue. Opening a card shows its full album.
help.browseGroup.play.title: Play or explore
help.browseGroup.sample.body: This page shows a random sample from the decade. Surprise me again reshuffles it locally. Back preserves the current selection.
help.browseGroup.sample.title: A random selection
help.browseIndex.decade.body: Choose a decade card to discover its albums. Years come from the tracks, with the album year as fallback. Unknown years are excluded.
help.browseIndex.decade.title: Choose a decade
help.browseIndex.find.body: Search or sort the groups, then choose a card to see its matching albums. Album totals follow the same merged sets as the album browser.
help.browseIndex.find.title: Find a group
help.browseIndex.open.body: Each card opens the albums belonging to that group. Back returns to your previous search and page.
help.browseIndex.open.title: Open matching albums
help.browseTags.find.body: Open a tag to see albums with at least one tagged track, then open an album to manage its tags or a single track's tags. Search, sort and page without loading every track into the browser.
help.browseTags.find.title: Find albums
help.browseTags.labels.body: Tags are custom labels attached to tracks. These cards include empty tags and show the matching album and track totals. Archived labels are marked.
help.browseTags.labels.title: Your iBroadcast labels
help.browseTags.manage.body: New tag creates an empty label after review. Inside a tag, Rename and Delete affect that label throughout iBroadcast. Deleting a tag keeps your tracks. Tags can be hidden or reordered in Settings like other optional shortcuts.
help.browseTags.manage.title: Manage labels
help.browseTags.title: Tags
help.browseUploads.albums.body: An album appears when at least one of its tracks belongs to this upload folder or day. The same album can appear in several groups; opening, playing or queuing it uses the complete album. Search also finds matching track titles and artists within this group. Sort and page the existing album cards; Back restores your group, search and page. No bulk editing or deletion is offered here.
help.browseUploads.albums.title: Albums in this group
help.browseUploads.find.body: Search full upload paths or stored upload days, sort and page the results. Missing information appears under Unknown. Folder case and separators are kept as stored; dates and times are not converted to another time zone.
help.browseUploads.find.title: Find an upload group
help.browseUploads.history.body: These optional shortcuts are off by default. Enable them under Settings → Interface → Sidebar. Upload folders are historical paths reported by iBroadcast, not local folders or playlist folders. Nothing on your disk is opened or scanned.
help.browseUploads.history.title: Your upload history
help.downloads.choose.body: Use Download album in an album's More menu, or select albums and choose Download. Adding a selection only queues it here; it does not fetch audio or change your playing queue.
help.downloads.choose.title: Choose albums
help.downloads.resume.body: Stop preserves completed files and matching streaming partials. Review and start again to resume. Existing unverified or modified files are kept, never adopted automatically. Selection and progress are session-local; folder options and integrity records persist. Avoid simultaneous downloads to the same folder from ibfetch or another Tagcast profile.
help.downloads.resume.title: Stop and resume safely
help.downloads.review.body: Choose a folder on the computer running Tagcast, quality and file source. Review download shows the exact selection and example filenames before Start downloads creates local copies. Free accounts use 128 kbps MP3.
help.downloads.review.title: Review before starting
help.downloads.source.body: Original downloads use iBroadcast's download service. Enable Download Updated Metadata in iBroadcast for its current tags. A visible Fallback note means the original upload was saved instead. The streaming source keeps the file's uploaded tags.
help.downloads.source.title: Current tags or the original upload
help.downloads.title: Downloads
help.duplicateCleanup.analyse.body: Analyse all albums applies the album page's Select suggested copies rules across your entire library, regardless of search or pagination. It reads stored metadata and prepares a local draft; it does not move tracks.
help.duplicateCleanup.analyse.title: Analyse all duplicate albums
help.duplicateCleanup.approve.body: Approve your selection before moving copies to iBroadcast's trash in batches. Current metadata and retained copies are checked before each batch, then the result is read back. Stop prevents further requests; uncertain requests are never automatically retried.
help.duplicateCleanup.approve.title: Approve and process
help.duplicateCleanup.compare.body: Prefer FLAC over MP3, then the newest upload in the same format. Uncertain copies remain. Review each repeated position, including differing titles. Uncheck an album or an individual proposed copy to keep it.
help.duplicateCleanup.compare.title: Compare and adjust
help.duplicateCleanup.title: Suggested duplicate copies
help.editing.draft.body: Change the title, primary album artist, additional album artists, year or genres. Type in artist, genre or composer fields to search existing library names, or use the arrow to browse. Selecting a genre or composer adds one whole label; typed semicolons still separate new labels. Click a name or use Up/Down and Enter; Escape closes the list. You can still type a new name. Keep each album artist separate. Selecting Various Artists hides additional album artist fields and clears those credits in the review while keeping track artists and track credits. Unticking restores the unsaved fields. Genres allow 200 characters per label and 20 labels per track; invalid input stays in the field. Applying the year to tracks is a separate choice.
help.editing.draft.hint: These fields appear in the album editor.
help.editing.draft.title: Edit your draft
help.editing.releaseYear.body: Also apply the release year to tracks in this selection copies the album year to its tracks in the reviewed draft. Choose the default under Settings → Interface → Metadata editing. The preference applies to new drafts; you can untick the album option each time. For selected albums, first enable Release year. Mixed disc years start unchecked. Applying a blank year or 0 clears track years; individual track edits take priority.
help.editing.releaseYear.title: Release year and tracks
help.editing.review.body: Choose Review draft to compare the before and after values. You can then keep editing or explicitly save the reviewed changes to iBroadcast.
help.editing.review.title: Review before saving
help.editing.selection.body: This header identifies the album, discs or albums by one artist included in the draft. Nothing is saved just by opening the editor.
help.editing.selection.title: Your editing selection
help.editing.suggestions.body: Online sources can suggest metadata and artwork. Metadata suggestions fill your draft. Cover changes have their own comparison and save action.
help.editing.suggestions.hint: Online suggestions are available when editing a single album.
help.editing.suggestions.title: Compare suggestions
help.editing.tabs.body: Edit album contains shared album fields and online suggestions. Choose Edit tracks for the track list, individual credits and lyrics. Switching tabs retains both drafts and makes no requests. Review draft includes metadata changes from both tabs. Lyrics keep their separate review and save.
help.editing.tabs.hint: Individual track editing is available for one album or disc set; bulk artist editing keeps its shared fields.
help.editing.tabs.title: Album and track tabs
help.editing.title: Edit metadata
help.editingTracks.details.body: Edit title, primary artist, year, number, genres and additional credits. Keep each performer and role separate. Individual changes take precedence over album-wide track edits. Review draft includes metadata changes from both tabs.
help.editingTracks.details.hint: Choose a track to show its form.
help.editingTracks.details.title: Track details and credits
help.editingTracks.lyrics.body: The track lyrics field reads iBroadcast first. Find lyrics explicitly searches LRCLIB if none are stored, including matching release-label variants when the duration is known. Timed results become ordinary text. Use these lyrics fills the separate field; Review lyrics and Save lyrics to iBroadcast require a separate confirmation and Premium. Original file tags stay unchanged.
help.editingTracks.lyrics.hint: Choose a track to read its lyrics.
help.editingTracks.lyrics.title: Lyrics
help.editingTracks.review.body: Review draft compares all album and track metadata changes before saving. Switching tabs does not change the save scope or start playback.
help.editingTracks.review.title: Review all metadata
help.editingTracks.select.body: Choose Edit beside a title. The list scrolls independently; disc headings are preserved for multi-disc sets. Selecting another track keeps the previous track’s valid changes in the draft.
help.editingTracks.select.title: Select a track
help.editingTracks.tabs.body: Edit tracks keeps the track list beside one track’s form. Edit album returns to shared fields and suggestions. Switching tabs preserves entered values and never saves or starts a lookup.
help.editingTracks.tabs.title: Choose what to edit
help.editingTracks.title: Edit tracks
help.favourites.find.body: Search this list, choose the page size, then play a track or open its album. The + menu offers queue and playlist actions.
help.favourites.find.title: Find and play
help.favourites.remove.body: The filled heart removes a favourite by setting its rating to 0. The track remains in your library. Thumbs-down replaces the rating with 1 after confirmation and removes the track from this favourites list. Rating changes are checked afterwards.
help.favourites.remove.title: Remove a favourite
help.favourites.tabs.body: The tabs switch between Tracks, Albums and Album artists. Searches and pages stay separate, and playback continues when switching.
help.favourites.tabs.title: Choose your favourites
help.favourites.title: Favourite tracks
help.favourites.tracks.body: This list uses iBroadcast track ratings of 5. It includes existing five-star tracks and changes made in other iBroadcast apps after reloading the library.
help.favourites.tracks.title: Your favourite tracks
help.guide.analyse.body: Analyse my library compares the reference with your loaded album metadata and saves the results locally. Opening this page does not start an analysis. No audio is scanned.
help.guide.analyse.title: Analyse when you choose
help.guide.decades.body: Combine decade buttons with search and matching status. Sort by the reference year or List order. Show matching details hides or restores the labels and link buttons on cards; your matches stay saved.
help.guide.decades.hint: The filters appear after an analysis is ready.
help.guide.decades.title: Explore by decade or year
help.guide.edition.body: Use Confirm match or Choose album on a card. Search your library if needed, check the artist and title, then choose Use this album. This saves a local link; it does not edit iBroadcast.
help.guide.edition.title: Choose your edition
help.guide.link.body: Change link or Undo link lets you revise your choice. Manual links survive Analyse again. Library or reference changes can require a fresh analysis.
help.guide.link.title: Keep or revise a link
help.guide.list.body: This selection is based on the book edited by Robert Dimery and covers 1955–2007. Compare it with the albums already in your iBroadcast library.
help.guide.list.title: Your listening list
help.guide.results.body: In your library means matched or linked by you. Possible matches need confirmation and do not count as found. Not found entries have a grey placeholder. A match does not establish that every track is present.
help.guide.results.title: Understand the results
help.guide.title: 1001 Albums
help.guideLink.find.body: Search your loaded library by artist or title if the suggested editions are not the one you want.
help.guideLink.find.title: Find your edition
help.guideLink.reference.body: This is the artist, album and year from the reference list. You are choosing the corresponding edition in your own library.
help.guideLink.reference.title: Check the reference
help.guideLink.save.body: Check the result, then choose Use this album. The link counts as found while its albums remain available. It changes no iBroadcast metadata; you can change or undo it later.
help.guideLink.save.title: Save a local link
help.guideLink.title: Choose an album
help.lyricsImport.files.body: Select or drop up to 100 UTF-8 or UTF-16 LRC/TXT files, at most 5 MB in total. The left column shows this album’s tracks; the right column shows imported files. Reading files stays local until review. Original music and lyrics files stay unchanged.
help.lyricsImport.files.title: Choose sidecar files
help.lyricsImport.links.body: Unique track-number and title matches are linked automatically. A disc prefix can distinguish multi-disc positions. Select a track and a file, then Link selected track and file to correct a match. Unlink keeps a track out of the import. Ambiguous matches stay manual. LRC timing markers are removed; ordinary lyrics text is saved.
help.lyricsImport.links.title: Check the links
help.lyricsImport.review.body: Review linked lyrics checks fresh iBroadcast lyrics for linked tracks only. Compare Before and After. Existing text is kept unless you choose Replace existing lyrics for that track. Save reviewed lyrics requires Premium and sends individual changes in sequence, preserving other userdata. Stop finishes the current request and its check. Errors or unconfirmed results stop remaining writes, with no automatic retries.
help.lyricsImport.review.title: Review before saving
help.lyricsImport.title: Import album lyrics
help.lyricsReview.save.body: Save lyrics requires iBroadcast Premium. Tagcast checks the track and its complete additional metadata again, sends once and reads the lyrics back. An uncertain save requires checking iBroadcast before reviewing again.
help.lyricsReview.save.title: Save once and check
help.lyricsReview.text.body: Compare Before and After. This changes only one track’s lyrics stored in iBroadcast; other additional metadata is preserved. A blank After removes the lyrics. Original music-file tags are unchanged.
help.lyricsReview.text.title: Review the text
help.lyricsReview.title: Track lyrics
help.lyricsViewer.known.body: The Lyrics label appears only after Tagcast has found text for this track. Opening this window uses that text without starting playback or fetching lyrics. No label can also mean the track has not been checked yet.
help.lyricsViewer.known.title: Known lyrics
help.lyricsViewer.source.body: The source is shown below the text: lyrics saved in iBroadcast, or a public LRCLIB result. Close or press Escape to return to the album.
help.lyricsViewer.source.title: Text source
help.lyricsViewer.title: Track lyrics
help.overview.metadata.body: Metadata health counts highlight missing or combined values. Follow a count’s link to inspect the matching albums or album artists before deciding whether to edit them.
help.overview.metadata.title: Explore metadata
help.overview.numbers.body: Overview summarises your collection and account using the loaded library. Album totals use the same displayed sets as the album browser.
help.overview.numbers.title: Your library in numbers
help.overview.title: Overview
help.playlist.addQueue.body: You can append the current queue to this playlist after reviewing the change. Adding an individual track or album is also available from its playlist action.
help.playlist.addQueue.hint: Queue additions are available for editable private playlists.
help.playlist.addQueue.title: Add your queue
help.playlist.contents.body: Tracks appear in the playlist's order, 100 per page. Search this playlist matches title, artist or album across every page using the loaded library. Original position numbers remain visible; clearing the search restores all tracks. Playback and editing still use the complete playlist (or the displayed page above 10,000 tracks). Playlists over 10,000 tracks can be opened and paged; Play this page queues only the current page. Full-content replacement stays limited to 10,000 tracks. Adding tracks and reviewed deletion remain available. Use + for individual queue actions. The cross at the right removes only that playlist occurrence after confirmation; library tracks and the current play queue stay intact. Removing positions is limited to playlists with up to 10,000 saved positions.
help.playlist.contents.title: Playlist contents
help.playlist.cover.body: Hover the cover or focus it with the keyboard to choose Change cover; the action stays visible on touch devices. Compare the current image with your file or image URL. Save explicitly, then wait for confirmation. Only this playlist artwork changes; track and album covers, playback and metadata history stay intact.
help.playlist.cover.title: Playlist cover
help.playlist.delete.body: Delete playlist requires a review. It removes only the playlist definition; all its tracks remain in your library. System playlists and folders cannot be deleted here.
help.playlist.delete.hint: Deletion is available only for editable playlists.
help.playlist.delete.title: Delete the playlist
help.playlist.edit.body: If all track choices stay checked, changing the name or description sends only the changed text. The review shows Before and After; every stored track position stays intact. Unchecking tracks prepares a full contents replacement instead. Both routes require confirmation and iBroadcast read-back.
help.playlist.edit.title: Edit details or contents
help.playlist.shuffle.body: Shuffle playlist replaces the play queue with the complete playlist in a newly mixed order. Each entry appears once per pass; the saved playlist and displayed positions keep their order. Play playlist restores ordinary ordered playback. Above 10,000 tracks, Shuffle this page uses only the current page, just like Play this page. Opening Help never starts playback.
help.playlist.shuffle.title: Shuffle playback
help.playlist.title: Playlist
help.playlistCover.compare.body: Choose a JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF file up to 15 MB, or an image URL. Compare Now and New before saving. This is a playlist cover; it does not replace the covers of its tracks or albums.
help.playlistCover.compare.title: Compare covers
help.playlistCover.save.body: Save explicitly and wait for iBroadcast read-back. If the playlist or account changed during upload, the image is not applied. An uncertain save needs a fresh review before retrying.
help.playlistCover.save.title: Save and check
help.playlistCover.title: Playlist cover
help.playlistFolder.manage.body: Rename or add references after review. Remove from folder unlinks only that reference. Delete is available only for an empty folder that is not referenced by another folder.
help.playlistFolder.manage.title: Manage the folder
help.playlistFolder.references.body: Open a member playlist or nested folder. These are playlist identities, never song IDs. Unavailable references stay visible and can be removed explicitly.
help.playlistFolder.references.title: Folder references
help.playlistFolder.title: Playlist folder
help.playlistImport.columns.body: Choose a CSV, separator, encoding and header setting. Confirm track title and performing artist columns. Album, album artist, duration, year and track number are optional. Numeric durations need seconds or milliseconds; mm:ss also works. Mapping Album title makes matching stricter; leave it unused to allow other albums or compilations. When multiple tracks match defaults to Choose manually; you can prefer FLAC, the oldest stored year, the first match, or FLAC then oldest year. Preferences apply only to copies matching all mapped fields. Unknown years come last; remaining ties use the lowest track ID.
help.playlistImport.columns.hint: Linking columns comes before matching. CSV cells are plain text.
help.playlistImport.columns.title: Read and link columns
help.playlistImport.matches.body: Results open on Unresolved records. Use Show to inspect automatic or manual matches too. A unique full-title and performer match is chosen automatically; an explicitly selected copy preference can also choose between fully matching copies. Match explanation says why a manual choice was needed; each suggestion lists its differences from the CSV. Multiple matching copies and invalid CSV fields are explained too. Search the loaded library or skip a record. Change match also lets you correct automatic choices. No online lookup or playback starts here.
help.playlistImport.matches.hint: Match the CSV first to see candidates and library search.
help.playlistImport.matches.title: Check every choice
help.playlistImport.pause.body: After reading a CSV or fetching a public playlist, Pause import saves its columns, source records, playlist text, copy preference and choices locally for this account. You can then upload missing tracks. Open Playlists → Paused imports and choose Refresh library & resume to recheck your matches. Pause again to update that saved copy. Closing a resumed draft keeps its last checkpoint; Remove separately reviews deletion. Pausing or resuming never creates a playlist.
help.playlistImport.pause.hint: Read a CSV or fetch a playlist first to make Pause import available. In the paused list, resume or explicitly remove one saved copy.
help.playlistImport.pause.title: Pause for later
help.playlistImport.progress.body: Once you have input or a draft, Close, Cancel and Escape ask before discarding it. Choose Keep importing, or press Escape in that confirmation, to continue with your choices intact. Only Discard import throws away the draft. Closing during playlist creation does not cancel the accepted request. Empty and finished imports close directly.
help.playlistImport.progress.title: Keep your progress
help.playlistImport.review.body: Choose more matches, or continue with only the selected tracks. Review matched tracks leaves unresolved records out and shows their count before confirmation. At least one track is required. Back to matches preserves unresolved rows so you can make more choices. Chosen tracks follow CSV order, with repeated IDs kept once at their first position. Confirm to create a new private playlist. Wait for read-back; an uncertain creation is never repeated automatically.
help.playlistImport.review.hint: The final review becomes available after matching. Existing playlists and music metadata stay unchanged.
help.playlistImport.review.title: Review and create
help.playlistImport.title: Playlist import
help.playlistImport.unresolved.body: Export unresolved records as CSV from the matches, final review or completion screen. The file includes all unresolved rows across every page, with original columns and order. Explicitly skipped records are excluded. Re-import recognises Tagcast's spreadsheet-safe text format automatically. Download before closing the import; the draft is temporary.
help.playlistImport.unresolved.hint: The export button appears when unresolved records remain after matching.
help.playlistImport.unresolved.title: Keep unresolved records
help.playlistImport.url.body: Playlist URL accepts public Deezer playlists and experimental ListenBrainz playlists. Paste a supported link and explicitly choose Fetch playlist. No source login or audio download is used. Fetching validates the complete list; blocked, private, oversized or incomplete responses show an error rather than preparing a partial import. Deezer respects its switch in Settings. After fetching, the same columns, matching, preferences, pause and final review are used. Album is available but not mapped by default. CSV cells containing links are never followed.
help.playlistImport.url.hint: Open Playlist URL from Playlists to fetch a public playlist. Opening this Help never fetches anything.
help.playlistImport.url.title: Public playlist URL
help.playlistOrder.find.body: Search title, artist or album across the whole playlist, including positions on other pages. Search keeps your unsaved moves. Result numbers and Move to position refer to the complete current draft. Drag and arrow moves also use that full order, including hidden tracks. Clear the search to see every position again.
help.playlistOrder.find.title: Find a track
help.playlistOrder.move.body: Drag a handle to the insertion line for a nearby move. With the handle focused, use Up or Down. Move to position accepts any position in the whole playlist, including another page. Repeated and unavailable tracks remain separate positions.
help.playlistOrder.move.title: Move saved positions
help.playlistOrder.save.body: Save order sends only the reviewed order, then checks it in iBroadcast. Cancel or Close discards the local changes. The playing queue stays intact. If the playlist changed elsewhere, reopen it before trying again; uncertain writes are not repeated.
help.playlistOrder.save.title: Save or cancel
help.playlistOrder.title: Playlist order
help.playlistReview.change.body: Check the name, destination and selected contents before confirming. Folder reviews add or remove playlist references; ordinary playlist reviews operate on tracks. Closing cancels an unsent draft.
help.playlistReview.change.title: Review the change
help.playlistReview.confirm.body: Confirm once, then wait for a fresh read-back. An uncertain request is not repeated automatically. System playlists stay protected; music files are never deleted by folder or playlist-definition operations.
help.playlistReview.confirm.title: Confirm and wait
help.playlistReview.title: Playlist review
help.playlists.create.body: Choose Create playlist to create a private playlist. You review its name and contents before it is sent to iBroadcast.
help.playlists.create.title: Create a playlist
help.playlists.folders.body: Create an empty folder, then review additions, removals and name changes. Removing a reference leaves its playlist and music intact. Search finds nested playlists too. Folder loops are blocked; only empty folders without parent references can be deleted.
help.playlists.folders.title: Playlist folders
help.playlists.list.body: Browse and search your iBroadcast playlists using the loaded library, without an online check each time. Reload library retrieves changes made elsewhere; saves still check and read back fresh data. Choose cards or list with the view buttons; this browser remembers the choice. The list shows covers, names, active track counts and duration, with unavailable tracks and unknown times labelled. Open a playlist to see its tracks in order. Open folders to browse their playlist references. System playlists remain managed by iBroadcast.
help.playlists.list.title: Your playlists
help.playlists.paused.body: Paused imports holds up to 10 locally saved CSV imports / 64 MB for this account, including after restart. Refresh library & resume retrieves new uploads and checks matches again. It keeps unchanged manual choices and skips, while changed choices need review. No playlist is created until you approve a new final review.
help.playlists.paused.title: Paused imports
help.playlists.title: Playlists
help.recentlyPlayed.again.body: Play a track, open its album or use its + menu for queue and playlist actions. Listening history is separate from metadata Change history.
help.recentlyPlayed.again.title: Listen again
help.recentlyPlayed.list.body: This is iBroadcast's recent tracks playlist, including plays reported by other devices. The most recent track is first and each track appears once. iBroadcast provides no play timestamps in this list.
help.recentlyPlayed.list.title: Your recent listening
help.recentlyPlayed.search.body: Search and page through the current list. Refresh from iBroadcast fetches the latest ordering. This page is available while optional play reporting is enabled.
help.recentlyPlayed.search.title: Search or refresh
help.recentlyPlayed.title: Recently played
help.review.compare.body: Read the proposed changes and check which albums and tracks they affect. Only changed, supported fields are sent.
help.review.compare.title: Check before and after
help.review.save.body: The save button sends your reviewed changes. Tagcast checks current values before writing and reads accepted changes back afterwards. A save can partly succeed; read the result before trying again.
help.review.save.title: Save and check the result
help.review.title: Review your draft
help.review.warnings.body: Warnings can block changes or require attention. Keep editing returns to your draft without saving it.
help.review.warnings.title: Read warnings
help.settings.albumInformation.body: Optional English album background text from TheAudioDB is off by default and independent of artist biographies and 1001 Albums. After saving, visiting an album checks its local cache first, then fetches missing or outdated text for one exact artist and full title. Text is reused for 30 days and never changes your metadata.
help.settings.albumInformation.hint: Album information needs the local Tagcast server.
help.settings.albumInformation.title: Album information
help.settings.biographies.body: Optional English biographies from TheAudioDB are off by default. After enabling and saving, visiting an album artist checks the local cache first. Only missing or outdated text needs an external lookup of that artist's name. Biographies do not edit your music metadata.
help.settings.biographies.hint: Artist biographies need the local Tagcast server.
help.settings.biographies.title: Artist biographies
help.settings.discovery.body: Enable 1001 Albums here and save to show its shortcut. Analysis starts only when you choose it on that page; enabling the feature does not scan your library. This setting controls the discovery page; bundled album background texts stay available when it is off.
help.settings.discovery.hint: Discovery preferences need the local Tagcast server.
help.settings.discovery.title: Discovery
help.settings.exportChanges.body: Download the change history saved in this browser as a JSON file. Export is available after a change has been recorded, and does not save pending settings. You can also export from Change history.
help.settings.exportChanges.title: Export changes
help.settings.find.body: Use the categories to find settings. Switching categories preserves pending server choices. Browser Back and Forward follow the visited categories. Immediate preferences are applied locally; server preferences require Save changes. Discard changes resets only the pending server choices.
help.settings.find.title: Find a preference
help.settings.gapless.body: An optional experiment for consecutive album tracks played in order. Preparation can delay starting or seeking near the end. Shuffle and playlists use normal playback. The switch applies on the next track; expand the technical details in Playback for supported formats and limitations.
help.settings.gapless.title: Gapless playback
help.settings.interface.body: Restore the library information banner. Sidebar shortcuts are listed directly below, with no disclosure to open. These choices apply immediately in this browser.
help.settings.interface.title: Interface
help.settings.libraryMetadata.body: Prepare JSON or a ZIP of linked CSV tables from the full loaded library, including separate artists, roles and credit phrases. Then choose Download. Optional tags, playlists and local favourites are included when available; the manifest reports missing data. This does not fetch tracks, save settings or change iBroadcast.
help.settings.libraryMetadata.title: Library metadata
help.settings.nowPlayingLyrics.body: Open Now playing in the sidebar to follow lyrics beside the current track, or choose Lyrics in the large player. iBroadcast only is the default. An online option checks Unison, then LRCLIB if no usable result is available and that source is enabled. Only title, track artist, album and duration are sent while the lyrics view is visible. Online text is temporary and never fills the editor. The softened cover background is always shown when artwork is available.
help.settings.nowPlayingLyrics.title: Now playing lyrics
help.settings.nowPlayingView.body: Choose Fullscreen or In app window for the expanded player. The choice is remembered in this browser or desktop profile and applies the next time you open Now playing. Playback and the queue stay unchanged.
help.settings.nowPlayingView.title: Now playing view
help.settings.playback.body: Choose streaming quality separately from the stored file format. Optional play reporting and queue synchronisation are independent and off by default. Save server preferences with the Save button.
help.settings.playback.hint: Playback preferences need the local Tagcast server.
help.settings.playback.title: Playback and devices
help.settings.sidebar.body: Show, hide and reorder optional shortcuts. Album artists, Albums, Change history and connection controls remain available. Restore default sidebar resets the layout.
help.settings.sidebar.title: Sidebar
help.settings.sources.body: Select online sources individually, then Save. All are selected by default; sources requiring a key still need one. Disabling keeps saved keys and skips metadata and image suggestions. Biographies and album information have separate switches. Automatic lookup sends album and artist names only to selected, available sources. Update settings control release checks; updates are installed manually.
help.settings.sources.hint: Source and update preferences need the local Tagcast server.
help.settings.sources.title: Sources and updates
help.settings.spectrum.body: Choose Off, Next to the title, Over the cover or Along the top edge. The bars follow the music that is playing and replace the speaker in the playing row of album and playlist tracklists. Along the top edge uses Next to the title in narrow windows. The choice is remembered in this browser or desktop profile; playback, volume and audio output stay unchanged.
help.settings.spectrum.title: Player spectrum
help.settings.title: Settings
help.tags.changes.body: Keep as is preserves existing assignments. Add applies the label to the chosen tracks; Remove unassigns it. Choices survive tag search and paging. Archived tags cannot be added here because they may hide music.
help.tags.changes.title: Choose changes
help.tags.labels.body: iBroadcast tags are separate from genres. On an album, changes apply to its tracks, including every disc of the displayed set; track controls affect only that track. In Albums or an artist’s page, select complete albums and choose Tag… to manage up to 20 albums / 500 tracks together. The selection count shows partial assignments.
help.tags.labels.title: Your own labels
help.tags.review.body: Review tag changes before saving. New tag creates an empty label to assign afterwards. Rename and Delete affect the label throughout iBroadcast. Deleting a label keeps your music. Every write is checked and read back; there is no automatic retry or metadata Undo. Selected albums are deselected after a fully confirmed assignment; cancelling, errors and creating an empty tag keep the selection.
help.tags.review.title: Review and confirm
help.tags.title: Tags
help.tour.noTarget: The controls appear here when this page has content available.
help.tracks.actions.body: A track's + menu offers queue, play next and playlist actions. The heart sets the native track rating to 5; thumbs-down sets it to 1. Click the active control to clear to 0. Replacing a nonzero rating asks for confirmation. Dislikes do not skip or trash tracks. A format label describes the stored file, not the selected streaming quality.
help.tracks.actions.title: Track actions
help.tracks.open.body: Play a result to listen, or open its album to see the full track list and editor. Artist links open albums featuring that performer.
help.tracks.open.title: Open or play a result
help.tracks.search.body: Search titles, performers, albums or composers across your library. Results are paginated; narrow the search if there are many matches.
help.tracks.search.title: Search your tracks
help.tracks.title: Tracks
help.uploads.prepare.body: Enable Music uploads under Settings → Data & exports, save, and reconnect once to approve upload permission. Choose local files or a folder on the computer running Tagcast. Preparation reads selected files and checks identical uploads; it does not send audio.
help.uploads.prepare.title: Choose and prepare
help.uploads.progress.body: Pause waits between files. Stop interrupts a current transfer where possible. Already sent files may still arrive. Uncertain outcomes are not retried automatically; check iBroadcast before preparing again. Uploaded means iBroadcast confirmed receipt; Details explains the additional file-list check. After full success the old selection is cleared; New upload starts a fresh selection. Reload the library explicitly after processing. Local files, your playback queue and existing metadata drafts stay unchanged.
help.uploads.progress.title: Pause, stop and verify
help.uploads.review.body: Check filenames and skipped-file reasons. Only Ready to upload files are sent after Start uploads. Byte-identical files already in your account or repeated in this selection are skipped. Different tags count as different files.
help.uploads.review.title: Review before sending
help.uploads.title: Music uploads
history.clear.busy: Wait until saves and their checks have finished.
history.clear.storageFailed: Change history could not be cleared from browser storage. Try again when storage is available.
history.cleared: Change history cleared. Your library is unchanged.
history.empty: No drafts yet. Open an album to start editing.
history.export.empty: Make and review an edit before exporting the change history.
history.field.name: Title
history.field.title: Title
history.note.demo: Export the changes before closing this tab. Preview drafts are not saved to iBroadcast.
history.note.live: Saved changes are listed with their read-back status. Export the changes if you want a record of this session.
history.reviewRestConnect: Connect your iBroadcast account to save these changes.
library.badge.duplicatedTitle: Repeated track numbers on the same disc. Open the album to compare the tracks.
library.empty.loading: Checking your iBroadcast library… A full download of a large library can take half a minute.
library.empty.noMatch: No albums match your filters. Try another artist or search.
library.load.unchanged_one: Loaded {{count, number}} albums. Nothing changed in iBroadcast since the last download.
library.load.unchanged_other: Loaded {{count, number}} albums. Nothing changed in iBroadcast since the last download.
library.loading.cable: Untangling the world’s longest imaginary headphone cable…
library.loading.cloud: Convincing the cloud to give your music back…
library.loading.counting: Counting your albums. No judgement. Mostly.

library.page.subtitleArtist: Open an album to listen, or select albums by this artist to edit, tag or move to the trash together.
library.page.subtitleDemo: Browse your collection, play an album, and edit its details when you choose.
library.page.subtitleDuplicates: Albums with repeated track numbers on the same disc, including tracks whose titles differ. Open an album to compare the copies.
library.page.subtitleLive: Browse your collection, play an album, or select albums to tag, merge or move to the trash together.
library.page.title: Your albums.
library.selection.helpArtist: Selection is limited to this artist
library.selection.helpDemo: Open an album to see its tracks and listen
library.selection.helpLive: Select albums to tag, merge or move to the trash together
listening.empty.description: Choose an album to start listening. Your music will appear here when you press Play.
listening.empty.title: Your queue is empty
listening.meter.label: Live audio visualisation (uncalibrated)
listening.settings.note: Now playing stays above the scrolling sidebar. Favourites and dislikes are in Now playing; Sound is beside Settings. Visualisations use the playing audio and are unavailable in unsupported browsers or with reduced motion.
listening.settings.open: Open Now playing from the cover
lookup.panel.heading: Suggestions
lookup.panel.hint: Click a year or genre to put it in the form; Shift-click a genre to add it to the others. Nothing is saved until you review.
lookup.results.needsServer: Online sources need the Tagcast server. Start it with {{command}}.
lookup.results.pressSearch: Press Search to look this album up.
lookup.results.sourcesChanged: Source settings changed. Press Search to refresh suggestions.
lookup.suggestion.score: How well the title and artist match
lookup.suggestion.useAllTitle: Use these genres, the first as the main genre
lyrics.check.failed: Lyrics check stopped: {{error}} Results already read are kept.
lyrics.check.stopped_one: Stopped after {{checked}} of {{count}} tracks. Results already read are kept.
lyrics.check.stopped_other: Stopped after {{checked}} of {{count}} tracks. Results already read are kept.
lyrics.check.tooMany: Album lyrics checks support up to 100 tracks. Check individual tracks in Edit tracks or Now playing for this album.
lyrics.editor.note: Save lyrics separately after review. Other track fields and additional metadata stay as they are.
lyrics.heading: Lyrics
lyrics.note.instrumental: LRCLIB marks this recording as instrumental.
lyrics.note.notCached: No lyrics stored in iBroadcast. Find lyrics sends this track’s title, artist, album and known duration to LRCLIB.
lyrics.review.intro: Change only this track’s lyrics in iBroadcast. Additional metadata and music files stay unchanged.
lyrics.review.saveFailed: {{error}} This request will not be sent again. Close this review and check lyrics again before retrying.
lyrics.review.saved: Lyrics saved and confirmed in iBroadcast.
lyricsImport.match.drop: Drop files anywhere in this dialog. Up to 100 files / 5 MB.
lyricsImport.match.fileNotLinked: Not linked · choose a track and link manually
lyricsImport.match.intro: Match files to this album. Automatic links require a unique track number and title. You can link other files manually.
lyricsImport.match.note: LRC timing markers are removed. Original files stay unchanged. Existing lyrics are checked during review.
lyricsImport.match.preview: Selected file preview · ordinary lyrics text
lyricsImport.match.previewEmpty: Choose a file on the right to preview its lyrics.
lyricsImport.review.intro: Check the complete Before and After text. Existing lyrics are kept unless you explicitly choose replacement.
lyricsImport.review.replace: Replace existing lyrics for this track
lyricsImport.save.noRetry: No request will be retried automatically.
lyricsImport.save.stopped: Stopped; remaining changes were not sent.
lyricsImport.status.back: Adjust the links, then review the current lyrics again.
lyricsImport.status.linked: {{linked}} linked. Check the links, then review existing and imported text.
lyricsImport.status.reviewReady: Review ready. Nothing has been saved. Tracks without a linked file stay unchanged.
lyricsImport.status.start: Choose or drop LRC/TXT files. Nothing is saved until you review and confirm.
lyricsImport.status.stopping: Stopping after the current request. Accepted saves still finish their check.
lyricsImport.title: Import lyrics · {{album}}
lyricsImport.tooManyFiles: Choose up to 100 lyrics files, at most 5 MB in total.

themeEditor.help.sharing: Contrast checks cover representative colour pairs, not every possible screen. Use the text fields to enter six-digit hex colours, for example #246276. Reset arrows restore individual colours. Import/export shares one theme as a small JSON file with its name, base palette and Light/Dark colour overrides. Export includes the current valid draft, without saving it. Import creates a new preview; choose Save theme or Save & use to keep it. Existing themes, account details and other settings are never included or replaced.
themeEditor.help.variants: Each theme has separate Light and Dark colours. Auto follows your system as before. Your draft stays here while you browse; saving is explicit. The built-in palettes are never overwritten. Warning/error colours keep their meaning. Native audio controls, system output pickers and window borders follow browser or operating-system styling.

uploads.guide.heading: How uploads work & privacy
uploads.guide.pause: Pause takes effect between files. Stop interrupts the current transfer where possible. A file already sent may still arrive. Uncertain uploads are never automatically sent again. Check iBroadcast before preparing those files again.
uploads.guide.preparation: Preparation checks supported formats and identical files already in your account. Nothing is uploaded until you choose Start uploads. Different tags make a different file, even when the audio sounds the same.
uploads.guide.privacy: Only the selected audio, its filename and relative folder path are sent to iBroadcast. Absolute paths and file hashes remain on this computer in the local hash index.
uploads.guide.session: Selections and progress are not restored after closing Tagcast. Scanning does not watch folders or remove music.
uploads.guide.tags: iBroadcast reads the original embedded tags. Tagcast metadata edits are not written into these files.
